title: Sake-Mirin Teriyaki Glaze
description: Mirin and drinking sake give this Japanese-style teriyaki a rounded sweetness and a clean, glossy finish.

ingredients.name: Sushi Chef mirin sweetened sake
ingredients.note: Estimate uses the label with 0 mg sodium and 50 calories per tablespoon.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 2 tsp total.

steps.title: Reduce the rice wines
steps.text: Bring {mi} and {sa} to a gentle boil in the HexClad for 3 minutes to concentrate the rice-wine flavors.

steps.title: Dissolve the sugar
steps.text: Whisk in {a}, {w} and {bs} and simmer for another 3–4 minutes. Keep the heat low enough that the sweet edges stay pale.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over warm salmon or chicken and use the rest at the table. A second thin coat clings better than a single heavy brushing.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 2 tsp coconut aminos in place of 6 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace the drinking sake with water and use half the mirin. Nutrition counts the full measured sake and mirin before evaporation. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 70 kcal, 0.1 g protein, 13.4 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 136 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 65 kcal, 0.1 g protein, 12.1 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.0 g fiber, 46 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
